expected_level_description: You can: - prepare monthly budget reports and explain the main variances - code costs correctly between cost centres, projects, and capital and revenue - support budget holders to understand and manage their budgets

You can: - build budgets and forecasts for a cost centre or project, including staff costs - update forecasts each month with known changes and risks - phase budgets so that spending profiles match delivery plans
You can: - explain the purpose of a business case and its financial section - collect cost information for a business case

You can: - apply the organisation's capital and revenue rules to everyday spending - explain how funding allocations and spending limits affect your area - recognise spending that needs approval from a funder or spending control
You can: - use spreadsheets well, including formulas, lookups, and pivot tables - maintain finance system data, such as cost centres, suppliers, and approvers - report and help fix system problems

You can: - process a range of transactions, including credit notes, refunds, and journals - reconcile supplier statements, bank accounts, and control accounts - resolve routine queries from suppliers, customers, and budget holders - spot duplicate, unusual, or unauthorised transactions and raise them
You can: - understand the financial impact of the work you do and how cost and budgets are created

You can: - listen to the needs of design and business stakeholders and interpret information - take part in discussions within a multidisciplinary team - be an advocate for the team externally, and can manage differing perspectives - shape and share communications relevant to the audience
You can: - describe the main parts of the health and care system and the services the organisation supports - explain why patient safety and confidentiality matter in your work
